fix_line: Ask MettleUp's own server for the newest version first, and wait a few hours after a refusal
title: Members who installed the app from GitHub may never hear of a new version when GitHub's free hourly limit is used up
how_often: when many phones share one internet address
expected: The version check should come from MettleUp's own server (as What's new already does), or wait before asking GitHub again after a refusal. MettleUp should see how often the check is refused.
what: The app asks GitHub's public service, without any sign-in, whether a newer version exists. That free service allows about 60 questions an hour for each internet address. Phones on the same gym wifi or the same mobile network address share that allowance. When it is used up, the app quietly shows no update, records nothing, and asks again on the next check with no waiting. Nobody at MettleUp is told. The What's new lines already moved to MettleUp's own server for a similar GitHub problem, but the version check did not.
